title: Replicating Knowledge Collapse: Do Models Converge on the Same Cultural Answers?

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Knowledge Collapse: Do Models Converge on the Same Cultural Answers?

**Problem:** Epistemic Diversity work found all models are less diverse than web search. Do models give homogeneous answers to value-laden questions, creating a single 'AI consensus worldview'?

**Direction:** Take contested/culturally specific questions using public prompt templates. Run ~12 models, cluster answers, and measure how many distinct positions the ecosystem offers vs a web-search baseline.

**Why it matters:** Homogeneous value judgments across all deployed assistants is a diffuse, long-horizon societal risk.

**Relevant context:** Epistemic Diversity and Knowledge Collapse (arXiv:2510.04226).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague/diffuse societal risk (value monoculture); little connection to catastrophic AI risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public prompts, clustering, established diversity metrics; accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused replication measuring distinct positions vs web baseline.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public prompts/models, no lab data; neglected long-horizon societal angle.

novelty.reasoning: Largely a replication of the cited Epistemic Diversity / knowledge-collapse work.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Knowledge-collapse/value-homogeneity directly studied by the cited paper.
